# Radical preimages generated by actual root and centralizer intersections

This internal support unit works over a local domain with a smooth affine
geometrically connected integral group, connected reductive generic group,
and an actual compatible integral split torus identifying a maximal split
torus of the generic group. For every represented unipotent radical of the
special fibre, `RadicalRootCentralizerGeneration` states that its full generic
reduction preimage is generated by its intersections with the generic torus
centralizer and every full relative root subgroup.

`IntegralSplitTorusData.radicalRootCentralizerGeneration` proves this assertion.
It chooses coordinates for the integral split torus and a generic cocharacter
whose dynamic centralizer is the whole torus centralizer. Actual integral
radical-preserving opposite, centralizer, and positive dynamic factors exist.
The integral kernel-preserving ordered-root theorem refines each dynamic
factor into integral root factors remaining in the same radical preimage,
using the smooth represented radical quotient on the residue field. Generic
transport identifies these factors with the actual generic relative root
subgroups. The centralizer factor lies in the generic torus centralizer by
the chosen cocharacter. Their generic images multiply to the original point.
The reverse containment is immediate from the subgroup intersections.

This is derived support from the Library's integral split-torus coordinates,
generic cocharacter centralizer, relative root system, radical-preserving
triple factors, and local root-kernel generation. It does not yet identify
these radical root intersections with Bruhat–Tits positive root fixers and
does not assert a subgroup independent of the model or apartment subset.
